question: How does the MUTCD classify regulatory, warning, and guide signs by function?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD classifies signs into three functional categories. Regulatory signs give notice of traffic laws or regulations; warning signs give notice of situations that might not be readily apparent; and guide signs convey route, destination, distance, service, and other geographical, recreational, or cultural information. This functional classification is a mandatory (Standard) definition, and it carries through to combined-sign requirements (e.g., regulatory or warning panels incorporated within guide signs must keep their distinctive color schemes). Standards (mandatory): - "Signs shall be defined by their function as follows: A. Regulatory signs give notice of traffic laws or regulations. B. Warning signs give notice of a situation that might not be readily apparent. C. Guide signs show route designations, destinations, directions, distances, services, points of interest, and other geographical, recreational, or cultural information." - "When regulatory messages are incorporated within a guide sign, they shall be on a rectangular panel with a black legend on a white background. When warning messages are incorporated within a guide sign, they shall be on a rectangular panel with a black legend on a yellow background." - "A combination of guide and regulatory signs shall be used in advance of and at the initial entry point and all intermediate entry points from general-purpose lanes or facilities to contiguous, barrier-separated, and buffer-separated preferential lanes where access between the preferential and general-purpose lanes is restricted to designated locations." Guidance (recommended): - Signs should be individually installed on separate posts or mountings except where one sign supplements another (among other listed exceptions), reflecting that signs of different functions are generally installed separately. Support (informational): - A changeable message sign (CMS) is a traffic control device at all times, and its regulatory, warning, and guidance messages fall under the same MUTCD provisions as the corresponding conventional sign categories except as stated otherwise in Chapter 2L. - Examples of regulatory and warning signs used together (with guide signs addressed separately in Section 2D.39) are illustrated for roundabouts in Figures 2B-21 through 2B-24. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2 shows height and lateral-location examples for different functional sign types, including regulatory (STOP, Speed Limit), warning (curve with advisory speed plaque), and guide (freeway/expressway and overhead street-name) signs. - [Image 2] Figure 2A-3 shows typical placement of regulatory STOP and YIELD signs at various intersection configurations. - [Image 3] Figure 2A-4 relates to Chapters 2B and 2C, which cover regulatory signs and warning signs respectively. - [Image 4] Table 2C-3 provides advance placement distances specifically for warning signs, illustrating the distinct application of the warning-sign function. - [Image 5] Page 23 (table of contents) shows Chapter 2B covering regulatory signs and Chapter 2C covering warning signs and object markers, organized by sign function. - [Image 6] Page 9 (table of contents) shows temporary traffic control chapters likewise organized into regulatory (Chapter 6G) and warning (Chapter 6H) sign categories. - [Image 7] Page 85 (Table 2A-2) shows how sign colors are assigned by functional type—e.g., regulatory (black/red on white), warning (black on yellow), and guide (white on green). - [Image 8] Page 162 (Figure 2B-23) illustrates regulatory and warning signs together at a two-lane roundabout, with guide signs referred to Section 2D.39. Citations: - Section 2A.03 Standard §1 (p.40) - Section 2F.12 Standard §11 (p.392) - Section 2G.10 Standard §12 (p.422) - Section 2A.13 Guidance §6 (p.57) - Section 2L.01 Support §3 (p.510) - Section 2B.51 Support §6 (p.123) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Figure 2A-4 (p.50) - Table 2C-3 (p.152) - Page 23 - Page 9 - Page 85 - Page 162
gold_answer: Regulatory signs give notice of traffic laws or regulations. Warning signs give notice of a situation that might not be readily apparent. Guide signs show route designations, destinations, directions, distances, services, points of interest, or other geographical, recreational, or cultural information.
